svg.aria-label: What's in the box for the kitchen-sink rebuild. A box holds five rows, one per issue in the set. At its foot, drawn as the floor everything stands on, FIX-1429: the file-declared workforce served over the app's real HTTP route, which today reaches zero compiled chunks after a production build. Above it, FIX-1475, durable hire: hire a team, redeploy, it is still there, as org-scoped state on the Postgres the app already uses. Then FIX-1476, channels and boards: one family, one named instance, and a seat that drains a named subset, with a warning for a board nobody watches. Then FIX-1477, both UI shapes shipped: inline and resource-backed components as client-package exports, which the app only consumes. Then FIX-1478, one recipe per job: the patterns dependency dropped wherever Workforce covers the surface. A boundary line under the box reads: kitchen-sink is a consumer. Nothing here ships an API only it can call. To the right, composed in by the app: its own channel kinds as CHANNEL.md flow factories rather than new Layer 1 types, and its own seat files as the authoring path. Below that, consumed and not owned: the W3 floor FIX-1351, landed; the W4 first cut FIX-1407, landed; and the Postgres persistence the app already runs on. Below that a note says the set is open and a child filed later inherits every rule. Finally, below a fence, what is not built: no kitchen-sink-only durable store and no in-memory-only roster; no kitchen-sink-only UI API and no third Workforce UI package; no hired seat inside supervisor or any pattern factory; no Agent, Team, Channel or Board as a Layer 1 type; no ambient all-boards drain; no runtime channel-admin verbs, which are parked as FIX-1415; no nested sessions as the work control plane; and no Lab product inside the kitchen-sink, since DevForce and CyberForce run beside it.
